title: Renewal & Expansion - Oakridge Capital
summary: Customer is happy with current performance but wants to expand capacity and add an EU region for data residency. Discussed dedicated reserved capacity sizing, pricing for 24-month extension, and a short performance benchmark pilot. Security/SSO and SOC2 docs requested. Next steps: pricing, pilot plan, schedule hands-on benchmark with SE.
next_steps: Jordan to send updated pricing for 24-month reserved capacity + region add-on by 2026-03-09
Priya to schedule benchmark window and share test plan by 2026-03-06
Oakridge to confirm projected q3 qps and compliance reqs by 2026-03-10
action_items: Jordan Lee - Send updated pricing and term sheet for 24mo reserved capacity and EU region add-on (due 2026-03-09)
Priya Nandakumar - Setup benchmark runbook + schedule 2-hour perf window with Oakridge infra (due 2026-03-06)
Ravi Patel - Share current traffic profile and top 50 prompt templates (due 2026-03-10)

header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Time: 15:00-15:42 UTC | Duration: 42 min | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (Redwood CSM), Markus (Oakridge Head Eng), Elaine (Oakridge CTO), Ravi (Oakridge Platform)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in — hope the month has been good. um Markus, Elaine, can you confirm this is mostly a renewal/expansion chat today?
[00:10] Markus: Yeah, yep. renewing in june, want to talk capacity and adding eu. big ask is data residency for some of our funds.
[00:20] Elaine: Also want to see the economics — if we commit longer can we get better unit price and dedicated capacity.
[00:30] Priya: Great. from a tech perspective we want to understand your qps and p99 targets so we can size dedicated pools. right now you're on hosted with some dedicated reservations, is that right?
[00:42] Ravi: correct, we have 2 reserved pools (3 gpus each) and fall back to hosted when bursty. p50 is fine, p95 around 220-240ms, p99 spikes up to ~900ms on long sequences.
[00:55] Priya: okay, thanks. long sequences cause the KV cache thrash — we saw similar with other customers — continuous batching helps but for consistent p99 you'd benefit from more dedicated capacity or bigger GPUs.
[01:10] Markus: what would you recommend? we were thinking 8 x smaller GPUs vs 4 x large A100s. cost is a big factor.
[01:20] Priya: tradeoffs — more smaller GPUs gives throughput but more network overhead and more warmup on KV. 4 x A100 (or equivalent) will reduce p99 and memory pressure. we can run a quick benchmark with your prompt mix.
[01:34] Elaine: and region-wise, we need eu-west deployment for the funds domiciled in ireland. is that a straight add-on or does it require a new private deployment?
[01:45] Jordan: we can add a hosted/dedicated pool in eu-west-1 as an add-on to your account; if you need private VPC peering or on-prem, that's a separate private deployment discussion. for EU data residency we can commit to region pinning for the model and logs.
[01:58] Ravi: this is good. what about encryption and KMS? SOC2 is fine but we also need CMEK.
[02:06] Alex: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private and for Dedicated we offer an integration path — we'll share the KMS integration doc. SOC2 and ISO artifacts are available.
[02:15] Markus: can you send those docs? procurement will want them.
[02:19] Jordan: yep will send SOC2 and KMS notes after this call.
[02:23] Priya: back to sizing — if your goal is 10k qps at peak with 95% p95 < 300ms, we'd propose a dedicated pool equivalent to 8 x A100-80GB (rough sketch) with autoscale headroom. if cost is tight we can propose 24-month reserved commit for discount.
[02:42] Elaine: 24 months sounds reasonable if the discount is material. what sort of discount band are we talking?
[02:48] Jordan: i don't have final numbers on the spot, we typically range 20-35% depending on commitment and region add-ons. i'll send a formal term sheet.
[02:56] Ravi: also want to understand fallback — if dedicated is saturated, what happens? do you failover to hosted and what's the latency impact?
[03:05] Priya: Failover policy can route to hosted model variants; there is higher tail latency and cost. we can also set automatic throttling or degrade to a cheaper quantized model for non-critical routes.
[03:18] Markus: can you quantify cost impact? we need unit economics to make a decision.
[03:22] Jordan: we'll include a cost comparison spreadsheet with committed vs on-demand and with/without region add-on.
[03:28] Elaine: about the benchmark — we need it to include our top 50 prompts and burst patterns. can you run inside our network?
[03:34] Priya: ideally we run two phases: 1) hosted baseline using sampled traffic, 2) dedicated pool test on identical hardware. for inside-network runs we can do VPC peering or temporary SSH to a runner — we'll detail options in the runbook.
[03:48] Ravi: timebox of 2 hours would be fine. we can allocate infra.
[03:51] Jordan: cool. i'll coordinate dates.
[03:55] Markus: side question — we heard about Redwood Optimize features that do batching suggestions and quant profiles. can that be part of the pilot?
[04:03] Priya: yes, Optimize can recommend batching/quant setups per workload; we'll include that in the benchmark and measure quality regression.
[04:11] Elaine: legal will want contract language for data residency and audit logs retention.
[04:16] Alex: noted — we'll surface the clause options in the term sheet and include audit log retention SLAs.
[04:22] Markus: any competitors you think we should be aware of if we push for private?
[04:26] Jordan: we see mentions of Anthropic and OpenAI for hosted API needs; Lambda Labs or self-hosted vendors for on-prem. we'll include a short competitive note.
[04:35] Ravi: perfect. so immediate asks: pricing + term sheet, SOC2/KMS docs, benchmark runbook.
[04:41] Jordan: yes. recap — Jordan send pricing & term by 3/9, Priya send runbook and schedule by 3/6, Alex send SOC2 + KMS notes by 3/5, Oakridge share traffic profile by 3/10.
[04:52] Elaine: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[04:55] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up in email with calendar invites for the perf window. end call.
questions: Can we get EU-hosted data residency for funds domiciled in Ireland?
What discount bands are available for 24-month reserved commit?
Can Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated?
How does failover to hosted affect latency and cost?
